_why: Migration numbers that two branches took at the same time, and BOTH applied to the shared database.

This is history, not a mistake waiting to be made. `app.schema_migrations` is keyed on the migration's NAME, so both files are recorded and both ran; renaming either would make the repository claim a number it did not run under, which is rewriting history to make a check green.

The check already refuses a duplicate whose files are not all applied — that is the case somebody can still fix by taking a free number. It could not tell the two apart on an EMPTY database, where nothing is applied by definition, so a fresh install was refused by the collisions of a history it had not lived through. This file is that evidence, written down once.

It cannot rot into permission: a collision that is not listed here still fails, and a listed file that no longer exists is reported. Adding to it is a deliberate act that says two numbers really did both run.
